claim: Hutter/Hoos/Leyton-Brown's fANOVA (ICML 2014) is the canonical origin of hyperparameter-importance variance decomposition in AutoML, computing marginal predictions of a random-forest EPM fit on Bayesian-optimization data.
stance_target: N6 crossed surrogate-class x optimizer factorial novelty
quoted_support: We first introduce a novel, linear-time algorithm for computing marginals of random forest predictions and then show how to leverage these predictions within a functional ANOVA framework, to quantify the importance of both single hyperparameters and of interactions between hyperparameters.

claim: In the Auto-WEKA (CASH) fANOVA experiment, model class was found to be the single most important hyperparameter, explaining 31-58% of performance variance across five OpenML datasets.
stance_target: N6 (weakens NONE FOUND slightly -- closest analog of a variance-attributed model-class factor)
scope_conditions: Auto-WEKA 768-dimensional hyperparameter space, 5 of 21 OpenML datasets, one SMAC run per dataset
quoted_support: Not surprisingly, the most important hyperparameter was the model class used.

claim: All Auto-WEKA fANOVA importance numbers in this paper are computed from data gathered by a single fixed search method (SMAC), never crossed against a second, independently-run optimizer to compare variance attributable to search-strategy choice.
stance_target: N6 NONE FOUND (no crossed model-class x optimizer factorial)
quoted_support: Top 3 most important hyperparameters of Auto-WEKA for each of 5 datasets, based on data from one SMAC run.
numbers: 25 repetitions (of SMAC runs for fANOVA runtime variance, not method comparison)

claim: TPE is named in the paper as an alternative search method Auto-WEKA could use, but is never actually run through fANOVA or compared against SMAC as a second factor.
scope_conditions: Section 4.2, background on Auto-WEKA's search methods
quoted_support: Auto-WEKA uses tree-based Bayesian optimization methods, such as TPE (Bergstra et al., 2011) and SMAC (Hutter et al., 2011), to search WEKA's joint space of models and hyperparameters.

claim: The paper's fANOVA interaction-effect machinery only ever quantifies hyperparameter-vs-hyperparameter interactions within one fixed search method's data, never a model-class x optimizer-class interaction term.
scope_conditions: Whole paper -- grep of 'interaction' (20 hits), all hyperparameter-pair interactions (e.g. Online LDA's kappa and S)
quoted_support: an interaction effect between S and κ, which is visualized
